2 19-08-2023 Heard Nitya Nand Neeraj, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and Mr. Jitendra Kumar Singh, learned A.P.P. for the State.
2.

The petitioner apprehends his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 281 of 2022,
registered under Section 341, 323, 406, 420, 504, 506 and 120(b) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of the Arms Act.

3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that in the year 2017, the complainant provided Rs.
1,12,80,000/- to the petitioners for recruitment of his son in army at the post of Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.52614 of 2023(2) dt.19-08-2023 MES through on Vivek Kumar on an agreement.

It is alleged that the complainant along with his sons went to the house of the petitioners and requested them to return his money, but they did not return his money and they also assaulted and intimidated him.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that petitioners are innocent and they have falsely been implicated in this case.

He further submits that petitioners have already return the entire amount to the complainant and in this regard, the complainant has acknowledged the same as would appear from the Agreement, as contained in Annexure-3 to the bail application.
5.
Learned A.P.P. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of pre-arrest bail to the petitioner.

6. Considering the nature of allegation made in the complaint petition as well as the fact that petitioner has brought on record by way of Annexure-3 claiming that the son of the complainant has received the entire amount, which was given to the petitioner.

The Court below is directed to verify the genuineness of the agreement, which has been brought on record by way of Annexure-3 to the bail application duly sworn before the Notary Public on 24.12.2020 and is directed to get it Patna High Court CR.
confirm from the complainant namely Mahendra Singh.

In case it is found that petitioner has returned back the entire amount to the complainant in that case, the petitioners, above named petitioner, are directed to be released on bail, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of four weeks from today, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Munsif-cum-J.M. 1 st Class, Arwal in connection with Complaint Case No. 281 of 2022, subject to the condition as laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Cr.P.C.
7.

The petitioners are directed to file all the requisite evidences in support of their claim that they have returned the entire amount within a period of two weeks before the learned Court below from the date of passing of the order and till then no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioners in connection with Complaint Case No. 281 of 2022.
(Purnendu Singh, J) manish/-
